home.headline: Front-end engineering with a designer's eye.
home.lede: Five years building production React, and ten years as a graphic designer before that. Loading states, transitions and micro-feedback are not polish added at the end. They are the product.

about.title: About
about.body: I spent ten years designing for print and the last five building front-ends. Today I work on a sports content platform: fourteen microfrontends over Module Federation, an AI canvas generation pipeline, production server-side rendering, and WCAG 2.1 accessibility.
about.aside: The design years are not decoration on a CV. They are why I notice when a layout is a quarter of a millimetre out, and why I think an interface without loading states is unfinished.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: Open to front-end and full-stack work across Europe.

projects.title: A catalogue of work.
projects.graphicsLede: Ten years of print and brand design, and five years of graphics made daily inside the Gipper platform.

podhod.short: Full-stack strength trainer on Cloudflare Workers and D1
podhod.long: A bilingual workout builder and tracker, built solo. A 1,324-exercise library, per-exercise progression computed by a pure engine, Google sign-in, and a CI pipeline that migrates the database before every deploy.

slovnicek.short: Offline-first PWA with a hand-written sync engine
slovnicek.long: IndexedDB is the source of truth, not a cache. The hard part is a bidirectional sync engine: last-write-wins with per-table watermarks, and pull deliberately ordered before push so a stale offline edit can never overwrite a newer server row.

rjecnicek.short: The same engine, retargeted to Croatian
rjecnicek.long: Slovníček rebuilt for a family member learning Croatian: a B1–B2 word bank extended with an electrician's trade vocabulary. Proof that a one-off app can be turned into a reusable product shape.

guess-the-band.short: Music quiz with a serverless API and difficulty stats
guess-the-band.long: Vercel Functions proxy the Deezer API server-side rather than exposing it to the browser. Every round and answer is recorded in Postgres to compute per-track difficulty. Anonymous play always works, and syncs the moment you sign in.

gipper.short: Fourteen microfrontends, an AI canvas pipeline, production SSR
gipper.long: The sports content platform I work on daily, used by thousands of organisations. A Claude agent interprets a natural-language request, the front-end renders offscreen React templates, measures text slots via getBoundingClientRect, and assembles a Fabric.js canvas.

job-feed-bot.short: My first Python project, running on a cron since day one
job-feed-bot.long: A job aggregator over five sources behind a pluggable source interface, notifying through a Telegram bot, running on a GitHub Actions cron every four hours with persistent dedupe state. My first project in Python, and the reason I now reach for it.

blog.title: Notes.
blog.lede: Writing about the things that were hard: sync ordering, measuring text before it exists, and the road from print design to production code.
